Just picked up an old Dell 990 MT PC (like this https://www.newegg.com/Product/Product.aspx?Item=N82E16883155304)) that has a 300 GB HDD and I want to replace it with a 500 GB SSD, It came with no DVD so how can I do this. As I understand the OS is paired with the PC so I can't do a copy and paste.

Has it got the Product Key (~25 character string) sticker on the side/back of the case? If so, you should be able to go Here and download a disc image. Then you burn that image to a DVD, install the SSD in the tower. Personally I recommend only having the SSD and optical drive connected during the OS installation, Windows likes to do screwy things with its system partitions and boot records when there are multiple drives. Even if you intend on using the traditional harddrive for storage, unplug it until windows is loaded. This way, you can also use the windows install on there in an emergency, like if your SSD dies. Boot to the DVD you burned, and it'll walk you through the install process, most of which is pretty boring.

The other thing I would do to prepare is make note of your sound, video and network card drivers, and if you can, have them downloaded before you do your reinstall. put em on a flash drive, and your post-install process will go more smoothly. If you don't know what you need, most dells have a service tag on them that you can look up on dell's site to get stuff for your particular hardware.
